statement: For every nondegenerate scalene Euclidean triangle T with side lengths 0 < a < b < c < a+b and c^2 >= a^2+b^2, and for either fixed planar orientation of T, there is no full-dimensional compact convex three-polytope all of whose facets are direct copies of T, where directness means agreement of the cyclic side-length order induced by the outward normal. Equivalently, every scalene triangle admitting such an orientation-preserving monohedral realization is acute.
contribution: A self-contained full-scope proof of the frozen orientation-preserving right-or-obtuse scalene remainder. Coherent boundary orientation forces every vertex degree to be divisible by three; Euler then supplies a degree-three star whose four vertices form a nondegenerate disphenoid, and exact coordinate identities force the common triangle to be acute. Georgiou's arXiv:2608.01109v1 states this remainder as open; a bounded current search found no later equivalent primary result, but no claim of priority is made.
